data.title: A poem about Orgoň – the last Slavic druid
data.excerpt: A poem by Lucia J. about Orgoň the Old, the last Slavic druid who did not accept the cross. When the army with the cross turns his temple to ruins, he curses the god Parom; Parom strikes him down with a thunderbolt, and ever since his soul has groaned imprisoned in a stone with strange runes at Orgoňova kýčera.

timeline.title: The cross or death
timeline.description: An army with the cross comes into the land and forces the inhabitants to give up the old faith; all accept the cross except Orgoň the Old, who remains well hidden.

timeline.title: Orgoň's curse
timeline.description: Orgoň, the Slavic druid, strikes his hand upon the wood as a hammer upon a wedge and curses the god Parom for allowing his temple to perish.

timeline.title: His disappearance and the imprisonment of his soul
timeline.description: The angered god of thunder Parom strikes with a thunderbolt; not a trace of Orgoň remains and his soul stays imprisoned in a stone with strange runes at Orgoňova kýčera.

mediaTexts.alt: A painting of a bearded man in a tunic and cloak, sitting on a boulder carved with signs in a forest beside a stone idol

blocks.text:
But how beautiful it is,
that Slavic nation,
which calls upon nature
and dwells beneath the Tatras.

But suddenly, in the distance,
an army draws near,
fear flashes from their eyes,
with God upon the cross.

“Come now, girl, accept the cross,
or you will pay dearly for it!
Throw the idol into the forest!”

And the girl nods her head,
she fears for her life.

They all accepted the cross,
they gathered up their things,
they went down into the valley
and left the forest behind.

All of them but one,
well hidden away,
Orgoň the Old.

“Parom, you god of heaven,
why did you allow this?
Your temple has turned to ruins.
Why have you forsaken us?”

He struck his hand upon the wood,
as a hammer upon a wedge.
“I, Orgoň, the Slavic druid,
I curse you, Parom!”

And as he spoke the words,
a thunderbolt struck him.
Truly he had angered
the god of thunder, Parom.

Not a trace left of him –
of his robe or of his belt.
Orgoň's soul –
in prison, in a stone.

In prison, in a stone
his soul is groaning,
with strange runes
that no one can master.

An uncommon stone
that looks quite common,
with strange runes –
Orgoňova kýčera.
